obligations.note: The new code in OutboundClient.url_for rewrites the statement-delivery base URL from https:// to http:// for any path starting with /archive/. That integration now makes outbound calls over plaintext HTTP, which violates the requirement that every outbound endpoint use https.

The INTEGRATIONS list is unchanged: core-banking, sanctions-screening and statement-delivery, with the same hosts. Each one appears in controls/payments/asset-inventory.json with an owner and a data classification.
The ENC-2 deviation is not covered by any exception: the register has none for ENC-2 or payments.integrations. Under EXC-1 the deviation is therefore not acceptable.

Ticket CHG-25625 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-11, before the change was opened on 2026-10-13. Its components (payments.integrations) cover the only touched file.
Sofia Santos, a change_approver for payments and not the author Aisha Bello, gave a code_review approval on the head commit.
Both approvals name the head commit 85a9e8fe, and there are no later commits.

run.json claims a CI run on the head commit on ci-runner-03, started 2026-10-13. The JUnit report it relies on is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-19, and its hostname is a personal workstation (dev-laptop-7.local). The report is not valid evidence from the change's CI run. The passing test_integrations_use_tls also does not reflect the http downgrade.
payments.integrations is security_sensitive. Security reviewer Kofi Mensah approved the head commit.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are touched, so no control_owner approval is required.
The change is not an emergency (ticket type standard, emergency=false), so no post-implementation review is due.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files. None of these is touched by this change, so no evidence lapses.

summary: The change makes statement-delivery archive calls use http instead of https, which directly violates ENC-2. No approved exception covers this deviation. The CI evidence is also unreliable: the JUnit report postdates the review time and comes from a personal machine, not the recorded CI runner. The ticket and approvals are otherwise in order, but the change must be rejected.
